paragraphs: I’m a PhD candidate in Mechatronics, Robotics and Automation Engineering at Kent State University, working with Dr. Tao Shen. My research is on quantum sensors and medical robotics, including assistive and wearable devices for rehabilitation. I also teach the Mechatronics, Signal and Electronics, and Circuits labs. I publish my work on quantum sensors and medical robotics.

Before the PhD, I worked in the field. I started with MRI and X-ray systems at Siemens Bangladesh and taught part-time at Daffodil International University. I then spent eight years at Philips installing and servicing CT and PET-CT scanners, and three years at Medtronic supporting the Hugo robotic surgery system in hospitals across Bangladesh and India. Along the way I helped expand the service business into Nepal and Sri Lanka.

During my MSc at BRAC University I published on explainable AI for medical imaging: deep learning models that show their reasoning when they detect kidney and lung disease in CT scans. That mix of hands-on hospital work and research shapes everything I build now.

events.title: Quantum World Congress 2026
events.summary: Nazmul attended Quantum World Congress 2026 from Sept 23 to 25, 2026, at The Hotel at the University of Maryland in College Park, Maryland, as part of the NSF I-Corps program. He did customer discovery, meeting industry leaders and entrepreneurs in quantum to learn what problems they face. He is a PhD candidate at Kent State researching quantum sensors and medical robotics. The congress site is https://www.quantumworldcongress.com/.
